objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with progressively worsening shortness of breath over the past 2 months.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Over the past two months my shortness of breath has been getting progressively worse, especially with activity rather than at rest. I also have an occasional dry cough, but I don’t have fever, chills, or night sweats.
Do you notice your shortness of breath worsens when lying flat, or do you wake up at night feeling short of breath?
Patient: Yes—when I lie flat I get more short of breath, and I sometimes wake up at night feeling winded.
Have you noticed any swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any swelling in my legs, ankles, or feet.
Do you have a history of high blood pressure, coronary artery disease, or any known heart conditions?
I don’t have a history of high blood pressure, coronary artery disease, or any known heart conditions. I’ve generally been healthy before this started.
How old are you?
Patient: I’m 60 years old.
Have you experienced any chest pain, pressure, palpitations, or lightheadedness, particularly during physical activity?
Patient: I don’t have chest pain or pressure, and I haven’t noticed palpitations or feeling lightheaded. My main issue is the worsening breathlessness with exertion.
Do you currently smoke, or have you smoked in the past?
Patient: Yes, I currently smoke about a pack a day and have been doing so for around 40 years. I don’t use any illicit drugs.
Have you noticed any recent unexplained weight gain, or do your clothes or shoes feel tighter than usual?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any unexplained weight gain, and my clothes and shoes don’t feel tighter than usual.
Have you ever been diagnosed with asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema?

Patient: No, I’ve never been told I have asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema. I’ve mostly just noticed the shortness of breath gradually getting worse over the last two months. I do get an occasional dry cough, but no fevers or night sweats.
Do you cough up any sputum or mucus, and have you noticed any wheezing or whistling sounds when you breathe?

Patient: I mostly have a dry cough with little to no mucus, and I haven’t really noticed any wheezing or whistling when I breathe. It’s mainly just that I get more short of breath with activity, and it’s worse when I lie flat.
Do you drink alcohol, and if so, approximately how many drinks do you consume per week?
I drink about one beer a day, and on weekends I sometimes have a bit more than usual. I don’t drink heavily otherwise.
